title: Homologous series; IUPAC nomenclature
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR02#t1 term and clue written for the game; OR03#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR03#t2 term and clue written for the game; OR03#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: OR02#N.4, OR03#N.4, OR02#N.7, OR03#N.7, OR02#N.9, OR03#N.10, OR03#N.11.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Homologous series
items.clue: A family of compounds in which each member differs from the next by CH₂.

items.label: Prefix
items.clue: Part of a name for a side group, such as methyl, ethyl, chloro or bromo.

items.label: Suffix
items.clue: The ending of a name that shows the main group: -ol, -al, -one, -oic acid.

items.label: Stem
items.clue: Part of a name giving the carbons in the longest chain: meth, eth, prop, but.

questions.stem: Which pair of compounds are successive members of the same homologous series?
questions.explanation: Both are carboxylic acids (CₙH₂ₙO₂) and they differ by one CH₂: ethanoic acid and propanoic acid.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂Cl?
questions.explanation: Longest chain four carbons. Numbering from the CH₂Cl end gives {1, 2}, lower than {3, 4}. Prefixes alphabetical.

questions.stem: The boiling points of four successive alcohols are: methanol 65 °C, ethanol 78 °C, propan-1-ol 97 °C and butan-1-ol 118 °C. Which statement explains this trend?

options.text: Longer molecules have more H atoms, so they form more hydrogen bonds.
Longer molecules contain more covalent bonds to break on boiling.
Heavier molecules need more energy to move, whatever the forces.
Induced dipole–dipole forces grow with chain length; each has one –OH.

questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding per molecule stays about the same. Each extra CH₂ adds electrons and contact area, so the induced dipole–dipole forces grow.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CHO?
questions.explanation: Four-carbon chain including the –CHO carbon, which is C1. The methyl is on C2.

questions.stem: Butane, C₄H₁₀, boils at −1 °C and is sold as camping gas. Dodecane, C₁₂H₂₆, boils at 216 °C and is a liquid in diesel fuel. Which explains the difference?

options.text: Dodecane molecules contain more C–C and C–H bonds, which must break before it can boil.
Dodecane molecules contain more hydrogen atoms, so they form more hydrogen bonds.
Butane and dodecane belong to different homologous series, so their properties differ.
Dodecane chains are longer, so the induced dipole–dipole forces are stronger.

questions.explanation: Longer chains have more electrons and more contact, so the forces between molecules are stronger. More energy is needed to separate them.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH(CH₃)CH₃?
questions.explanation: Six-carbon chain. From the left, the C=O is on C3 (from the right, C4) and the methyl on C5.
pent: five-carbon chain. -2-one: C=O on C2. 3-methyl: a CH₃ branch on C3.
